newsitem.title: UK: UK budget seen offering little to farmers.
newsitem.headline: UK budget seen offering little to farmers.

text.p: The 1997/98 UK budget presented by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Tuesday will make little difference to farmers' incomes, accountants Deloitte & Touche Agriculture said on Wednesday.

Changes in tax thresholds and rates would mean a benefit of around one stg an acre to a family partnership running a 500 acre arable farm. But this would be offset by increases in fuel tax and vehicle excise duty, it said.
"Overall this has to be considered a neutral budget for farming," the firm's Vincent Hedley Lewis said.
The budget contained 736 million stg in funding in 1997 to eliminate Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), or mad cow disease, from UK cattle herds.
It also gave support of 60 million stg for the UK's 60,000 upland farmers through increased Hill Livestock Compensation Allowance (HLCA) payments.
